Trump was in North Carolina yesterday barnstorming for the GOP Senate candidate there, Michael Watley.
American farmers have warned that high costs are affecting their crops.
But ranchers are warning beef may also be an issue in the midterm elections.
Ground beef costs $6.80 a pound on average. That's a buck more than when President Trump took office.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reports on how beef producers are being affected.
President Trump in August expanded the quota for lean beef trimmings that could come into the country under lower tariffs.
It was a move intended to lower ground beef prices, but it made life tougher for beef producers.
Scott Berger raises cattle in eastern Iowa.
That surprise with a very volatile market already with a tight supply hurts us really, really fast and really, really hard.
Trump's beef import policy has become an important topic in Iowa's closed Senate race.
And political strategists say it could also affect the state's House and gubernatorial races.
Several more major beef producing states are also midterm battlegrounds, including Nebraska, Texas and Kansas.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
The big tech company SpaceX has been pouring money into artificial intelligence.
NPR's John Ruich reports the company says that AI is now its biggest source of revenue.
In a quarterly earnings report, the company said its revenues were up 161 percent from the same quarter last year, beating expectations.
Revenue from AI leapt ninefold to $7.6 billion, or a little more than half of the total.
The company has its own AI model called Grok and it rents out data center space.
Starlink, its satellite internet business, grew its customer base during the period.
And the company says it's making progress with the recoverability of its heavy lift rocket called Starship.
Meanwhile, CEO Elon Musk says special committees at SpaceX and his EV company Tesla are discussing a possible merger.
John Ruich, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The United Nations is warning the world is not doing enough to stop climate change.
In a new report, the U.N. says the United States is one of the leading emitters of carbon dioxide and other planet warming pollution.
The report cites a big demand in electricity and it says more coal is being burned in the U.S.
President Trump has instructed coal fired power plants in the U.S. to remain open.
The president has signed into law Arizona's fourth national park.
From Arizona public media Katya Mendoza reports on the opening of Chiricahua National Park.
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum visited the 12,000 acre park that's known as the Wonderland of Rocks,
primarily made up of rock pinnacles called hoodoos.
Burgum says the department knows that there is a backlog of maintenance projects throughout the national park service system.
Congress is going to have an opportunity when they come back this November, December to pass the Great American Outdoors Act 2.0,
which will again represent the largest capital expenditures ever going towards the park service.
President Trump first signed the Great American Outdoors Act into law in 2020.
The most recently established park in the country was New River Gorge National Park and Preserve in West Virginia in 2020.
For NPR News, I'm Katya Mendoza in Chiricahua National Park.
Police in the Los Angeles suburbs say thieves have stolen nearly a million dollars worth of trading cards out of a FedEx truck.
Sports cards and Pokemon trading cards were among the items lifted last week.
No one has been arrested.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.
